sources.evidence: Issue of Cursor dated 18.11.88 with an item headed 'TUE niet in wereldfinale programmeerwedstrijd' naming the Ecole des Mines of Paris first and Rijksuniversiteit Leiden second at the European final held at the TUE on Saturday 12 November.

Issue of Cursor dated 11.11.88 with a news item headed 'Europese finale programmeerwedstrijd' announcing the final at the TUE on Saturday 12 November under the auspices of the ACM, with 25 teams from eight European countries.

erc-1989.notes: Both items are plain text only, with no newspaper name or publication date in the copy, so the year 1989 is not printed in either; the contest is identified by its content. Source 2 says nine problems, while the catalogue has a count of 4 problems.

sources.evidence: ANP item reporting TU Eindhoven first, Leiden second and Utrecht third at a European programming final in Eindhoven with 25 teams from nine countries; the text itself prints no year.

Newspaper item reporting TU Eindhoven first and Leiden second at a European programming final in Eindhoven with 25 teams from nine countries and nine problems in six hours; the text itself prints no year.
